sources.quote: Dear Bouncer, I am very glad you like Aurora Leigh. I think it simply 'intense' in every way. I am deep in a review of Symonds's last book whenever I can get time and the weather is too bright for fishing.
sources.context: Wilde to William Ward, [postmark 28 August 1876], Illaunroe Lodge, Connemara (MS Magdalen). The editors identify the book as Symonds's Studies of the Greek Poets and state that Wilde's review was never published. Wilde was twenty-one and had taken his First that July. The same week's letters contain the Todd passage.
sources.speaker: Oscar Wilde
sources.supports: That Wilde was reading Symonds closely at twenty-one, and that what he wrote about him did not survive into print.
sources.provenance: Repo PDF page 56; printed folio 31 confirmed on the rendered page image.

name: John Addington Symonds
bio: Writer and cultural historian (1840-93), author of Studies of the Greek Poets and, privately, of A Problem in Greek Ethics - one of the earliest sustained defences of homosexuality written in English. In the summer of 1876 Wilde, then twenty-one, was writing a review of Studies of the Greek Poets between fishing trips in Connemara. The review was never published.
bio_note: THE EVIDENCE IS ONE SENTENCE, read at the page, plus the editors' identification of the book and their statement that the review went unpublished. WHAT WOULD MAKE THIS FIRMER: the review text itself, which has not been consulted, and Symonds's own Memoirs and letters, which are outside this volume.
